clue.text: A bit of backbone is found in Washington

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Washington DC, the US capital, is shortened to DC

explanation.surface: A vertebra-related fact turns up in the US capital, as if Washington kept a spare piece of spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is the cushion of cartilage between two vertebrae, one small part of the spinal column.

clue.text: Unless I find out in an alternate way

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words that follow, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An instruction: unless you discover it by some other method.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is a conditional that means the same as the conjunction 'unless', introducing an exception.

clue.text: Shrove Tuesday treat flipped in piece of cookware

indicators.note: the treat is tossed over, so its first part ends up at the back

parts.note: Shrove Tuesday is Pancake Day in Britain, when pancakes are traditionally eaten

explanation.surface: A pancake being tossed in its pan on Shrove Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' moves the PAN of PANCAKE to the end. Shrove Tuesday, the day before Lent, is Pancake Day in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake pan is a baking tin, an item of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: On reflection, I might add, a cold-blooded killer

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is a remark added after a letter

explanation.surface: A speaker musing aloud adds an afterthought about some murderer with no feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I might add' stands for PS, a postscript; PS plus A is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a venomous snake, and snakes are reptiles, literally cold-blooded.

clue.text: Where junk might be lost

definitions.meaning: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship, found out on the ocean
bewildered, not knowing what to do

explanation.surface: Where discarded rubbish could go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' reads as rubbish but is the Chinese sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship on the open ocean is on the water; figuratively the phrase means confused or bewildered.

clue.text: Minestrone, say, served up without love is an unappealing liquid

indicators.note: the following letter is left out
in a down entry, served up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: minestrone is an example of a soup
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Soup dished up without affection is a nasty drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns SOUP into PUOS; 'without' drops the O (love).
explanation.definitionFit: Pus is the yellowish fluid of an infection, hardly an attractive liquid.

clue.text: Dodo could never manage this many stairs

definitions.meaning: the dodo was a bird unable to fly

explanation.surface: A dodo couldn't climb so many steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying through the air is beyond a flightless bird, and a straight set of steps between landings has the same name.

clue.text: Force multinational group to provide entertainment

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Coerce an international body into laying on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun is enjoyment or amusement, a synonym for entertainment.

clue.text: Trainees, one after another, in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: doing things in turns, each following the last

explanation.surface: Trainees auditioning for a role, one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Interns are trainees gaining work experience, often in medicine or offices.

clue.text: Announcing that woman's losing her hair after shaving head

indicators.note: the first letter, the head of the word, is shaved off

explanation.surface: A woman loses her hair after shaving her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing her hair' reads as part of the story but is one piece, a synonym for going bald; 'after shaving head' is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heralding something is proclaiming or signalling its arrival, as a herald would.

clue.text: Winds from the poles reaching lakes beyond the western border

parts.note: south and north poles, S and N

indicators.note: the letters after the leftmost one, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: Polar winds blowing over lakes past a western frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond the western border' takes LAKES without its first letter L, giving AKES.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or river that winds twists and turns, which is what something that snakes does.

clue.text: Suppressing gas? Common sense and hygienic!

indicators.note: holding something down within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a gas

explanation.surface: Holding back wind is both sensible and clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hides that 'gas' is the element argon, and 'Common sense' is a noun phrase, not a comment on the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanitary describes conditions that are clean and good for health.

clue.text: Action favourites return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A film or game cue: the popular stars come back for action.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken, a move towards a goal, an action.

clue.text: Notice wine making a comeback in summer

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice

indicators.note: coming back, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: An advert sees a wine returning to fashion in the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums, an adder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that adds up figures is literally one who sums.

clue.text: An aphid, surprisingly, is something you can feed to a fish

definitions.text: something you can feed to a fish

indicators.note: in an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An aphid, oddly enough, makes good fish food.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphnia are tiny water fleas, sold dried or live as food for aquarium fish.

clue.text: Nothing changes when this wheel turns

definitions.note: a spinning part of a machine, such as the blades of a helicopter; its name is a palindrome, so it supplies the letters too

indicators.note: the word stays the same however it is read, as a palindrome does
turning the word round to read it backwards

parts.note: a spinning part of a machine, such as the blades of a helicopter; its name is a palindrome, so it supplies the letters too

explanation.surface: A spinning wheel that looks the same however it turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' works twice: the wheel spins, and the word read backwards is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a turbine or helicopter blade assembly.

clue.text: After switching sides, bait government

indicators.note: left and right swap places: the L and R letters trade positions

explanation.surface: A defector tempts the government after crossing the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sides' swaps L (left) and R (right) in LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule is governance, the exercise of authority over a state.

clue.text: Freshwater char

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for a stream of fresh water
to scorch or blacken by fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like the freshwater fish, but it is the verb meaning scorch. A burn is a Scottish name for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a small stream is so called, and charring something means scorching it.

clue.text: Inland region up north gripped by violent outcry

indicators.note: held inside the following piece
violently disturbed, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Up north a rural district is in the grip of a furious protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges OUTCRY to COUTRY, and 'gripped by' puts N inside it to give COUNTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Upcountry land lies in the interior, away from the coast.

clue.text: Partial stone pot I stick somewhere inside

indicators.note: the answer sits at some point within the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook sticks a piece of stoneware somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Partial' as the indicator and 'somewhere inside' as the definition; 'Partial' is the definition (biased), and 'somewhere inside' signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial here means biased, and favouring relatives with jobs is a form of such bias.

clue.text: Empty characters show up in annual blast occasionally

indicators.note: only now and then, so every second letter is used

explanation.surface: Hollow people make an appearance at a yearly bash, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing a null is a character that stands for nothing, an empty value.

clue.text: Foolish reliance on Queen Elizabeth?

indicators.note: foolish handling messes the letters up

explanation.surface: It is silly to depend on the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Elizabeth' looks like the monarch, but the Queen Elizabeth was a Cunard ship; the question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen Elizabeth was a famous passenger ship, an example of a transatlantic liner.

clue.text: Reassembling his gun — a pain!

indicators.note: putting the parts together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting his firearm back together is a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe suffering, mental or physical pain.

clue.text: Stages features of 21D but not of 9

definitions.meaning: stretches of a journey or race
ladders stand on supports, while snakes have no limbs

explanation.surface: Phases of a journey, and something ladders have that snakes lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Legs are sections of a journey, and the uprights of a ladder are also limbs that snakes lack.

clue.text: Runs go up with these, and down with 9 in game

definitions.text: go up with these, and down with 9 in game
definitions.meaning: in the board game Snakes and ..., these carry counters up and the snakes carry them down

explanation.surface: In a children's board game you rise on one thing and fall on snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in hosiery is called by this name in Britain, and the game Snakes and Ladders uses them to climb.

clue.text: Called work great at first

parts.note: to run is to operate or function

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned, saying the work went brilliantly at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Having rung someone means having phoned them, as in 'I've called them'.

clue.text: Charlie enters transaction to get deposit

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie makes a deal to put money down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' reads as money in a bank, but it is the coating of limescale or tartar.
explanation.definitionFit: Scale is a hard crust left by water, a mineral deposit on kettles or teeth.

clue.text: Exceptionally unskilled actor

definitions.meaning: a film walk-on in a crowd scene with no lines

explanation.surface: An actor who is remarkably poor at the craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A background performer hired for crowd scenes bears this name, and as an adverb it means especially.

clue.text: Get rid of representative of the French first

indicators.note: the French word comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: Ditch the French delegate before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump is to discard or abandon something unwanted.

clue.text: Two graduates finding a reptile

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, and an MB, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A pair of graduates discover a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a venomous African snake, one kind of reptile.

clue.text: Paul, for example, assuming duct is a means of egress

parts.note: an airway is a passage carrying air

explanation.surface: Someone named Paul takes on a duct as an escape route, as in an action film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assuming' is a link here: ST takes on AIRWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is a way out of a building, a route of exit.

clue.text: Drawn from southern half of island nation

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower half is the southern part, so the top half goes

explanation.surface: Something taken from the south of an island country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'southern half of' keeps the lower half of TAIWAN in a down entry, dropping TAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks pale and tired, which is what wan means.

clue.text: One of the lads getting upset? Tough!

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down entry the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a boy is one of the lads

explanation.surface: One of the gang gets upset, and is told it's hard luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough!' looks like 'hard luck', but it is the noun for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough, aggressive young man, a hooligan or lout.

clue.text: Heating units from the Titanic?

parts.note: the ship was the RMS Titanic, Royal Mail Ship

explanation.surface: A question about the heating aboard the famous liner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Titanic's full title was RMS Titanic (Royal Mail Ship), so 'Titanic' gives RMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat used to measure gas supply in Britain.

clue.text: Befuddled hypnotist forgetting first language

indicators.note: confused, so the letters are jumbled
leaving some letters out of the mix

explanation.surface: A confused stage hypnotist forgets the first language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Befuddled' jumbles HYPNOTIST and 'forgetting' removes IST (first, as 1st) from the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Python is a widely used programming language for computers.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell accompanies a swamp-dweller

explanation.surface: A bad smell hangs about a creature living in the marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: The boa is a large constricting snake of tropical wetlands and forests.

clue.text: Second badger's a problem

explanation.surface: Another badger causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hitch or unexpected difficulty.
